title: record
description:
Client -> robot. Dataset recording verbs. Every verb draws exactly ONE record_status reply, so a client may await each one -- but replies carry no correlation id, so a client MUST NOT have two record verbs in flight at once. After a timeout, drop the waiter AND treat the next unsolicited status as unowned, or the correlation goes permanently off by one.

THE VERBS ARE NOT ALL SAFE. Read the per-verb notes below before wiring a UI to any of them: `session_discard` / `discard` / `discard_last` DESTROY recorded data, and on L2 `stop` closes the whole session rather than just the episode. Two verbs that look adjacent can be opposites.

Canonical lifecycle:
  session_start -> episode_start -> (episode_stop | episode_discard) -> ... -> session_end

The robot is resilient to a dropped session_start: an episode_start with no open session opens one implicitly.

action.description:
Semantics, and they differ per stack where noted -- verified against the L2 recorder (rpi5/media/recorder.py) and the L3 gateway (nori_gateway/protocol.py).

KEEPS DATA:
  session_start   open a collection.
  episode_start   open an episode (opens a session too if none is open).
  episode_stop    finalise and KEEP the open episode.
  session_end     close the session and keep it for shipping. On L2 a session that kept no episodes is removed, since there is nothing to ship.
  status          read-only.

DESTROYS DATA:
  episode_discard   finalise and DROP the open episode.
  session_discard   drop the ENTIRE open session, or -- if issued just after session_end -- the most recent one. On L2 this is shutil.rmtree. It refuses only if the session already reached `uploaded`. This is NOT a synonym for session_end; they are opposites. It is also NOT a legacy alias, despite riding next to them.

LEGACY ALIASES, retained because deployed clients still send them:
  start          L2/L3: open a session AND an episode.
  stop           L3: finalise the episode. L2: finalise the episode AND END THE SESSION. A client using `stop` between episodes on an L2 gets a different session than it expects.
  discard        alias for session_discard on L2 (destroys). On L3 it is folded into session_end (keeps).
  discard_last   alias for session_discard on L2, targeting the most recent session.

The divergence in `discard` between stacks is real and unresolved: the same verb keeps data on one model and destroys it on the other. Prefer the explicit canonical verbs and do not build a UI on `discard`.

task.description: Free-text task label recorded with the episode. Meaningful only on the verbs that OPEN something (session_start, episode_start, legacy start); ignored elsewhere.
